audit_scope.description: Trust model analysis for EIP-7825 (transaction gas limit cap), EIP-7927 (pre-merge history expiry), Cancun storage instructions (SLOAD/SSTORE/TLOAD/TSTORE), EVM arithmetic operations, and EIP-107 (safe transaction authorization). Covers transaction validation boundaries, P2P block propagation, storage operation security, and dapp-to-node RPC communication.

in_scope: Block validation for gas cap compliance

misclassified_entities.reason: Malicious Actor is a threat actor, not an external entity. In EIP-7825 context, attackers operate through the transaction submission interface (as a transaction sender) or P2P network (as a peer node). They should be modeled as threats against those interfaces.

Caller Contract is an internal EVM component. The contract that initiated a STATICCALL is part of the EVM execution context, not an external entity to the Execution Layer. Static context enforcement is an internal EVM security mechanism.

End User (human) in EIP-107 is the account holder approving transactions via popup UI. While human interaction is external to the software, this represents a UI trust boundary, not a network-level external entity to the EL. The user interacts through the browser, not directly with the EL.

Ethereum Node in EIP-107 refers to the local node that processes transactions. This is the EL itself, not an external entity. The dapp communicates with it via RPC, but the node is the system under analysis.

trusted_external_entities.name: Transaction Sender
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: Transaction submission via JSON-RPC (eth_sendRawTransaction) or P2P gossip
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Transaction senders are unauthenticated external entities. Any entity with a valid private key can submit transactions. The EIP-7825 gas cap (16,777,216) provides an upper bound on individual transaction complexity. All transaction fields are validated before acceptance into the mempool.

trusted_external_entities.name: Peer Network Node
trusted_external_entities.rationale: P2P network peers are untrusted. They broadcast blocks that may contain transactions exceeding the gas cap. The EL must independently validate all blocks received from peers, including checking each transaction's gas limit against the 16,777,216 cap. Peers may be malicious or running incompatible software.

trusted_external_entities.name: JSON-RPC Client
trusted_external_entities.rationale: RPC clients requesting pre-merge historical data (EIP-7927) are untrusted. After history expiry, the node may need to retrieve data from external sources (e2store, Portal Network, EIP-7801). Responses to RPC clients must indicate data unavailability when local data has been expired.

trusted_external_entities.name: Web Dapp
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Web dapps are untrusted external applications requesting transaction authorization. They communicate via postMessage to an authorization iframe. A whitelist of 43 read-only methods is enforced for unauthenticated iframe access. State-changing operations (eth_sendTransaction) require explicit user popup approval. eth_sign is explicitly prohibited.

boundary_edges.security_assumption: Transaction gas limit is validated against the 16,777,216 (2^24) cap before mempool acceptance. Transactions exceeding the cap are immediately rejected. This bounds the maximum complexity of any single transaction.

Blocks from peers are fully validated including checking every transaction's gas limit against the cap. Blocks containing any transaction with gasLimit > 16,777,216 are rejected entirely. This prevents peers from including oversized transactions in blocks.

After history expiry, pre-merge data requests may return errors or require fallback to external sources. Data retrieved from alternate sources (e2store, Portal Network) must be validated against known block hashes before being served to clients.

Dapp requests are sandboxed by the browser same-origin policy. Read-only methods are served via invisible iframe without user interaction. State-changing operations require explicit popup-based user approval. The 3-second account unlock window limits exposure time. eth_sign is explicitly blocked to prevent arbitrary data signing.

coverage_gaps: EXT-ATTACKER (misclassified threat actor), EXT-CALLER-CONTRACT (internal EVM), EXT-USER (UI trust boundary, not EL network entity), and EXT-ETH-NODE (the EL itself) were removed. The Cancun storage instructions and EVM arithmetic files had no external entities as they model purely internal EVM operations.
